PRENATAL GENETIC TESTING REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Sample Type: Chorionic Villi (uncultured)
Gestational Age: 12 weeks
Maternal Age: 32 years
Date of Collection: [redacted date]
Date of Report: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal screening for common chromosomal trisomies

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Chromosomes analyzed: 13, 18, and 21

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from uncultured chorionic villi. QF-PCR analysis was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. A minimum of four informative markers were analyzed per chromosome. Peak area ratios were calculated to determine chromosome copy number.

RESULTS
Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern observed
Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern observed
Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern observed

INTERPRETATION
PCR analysis showed normal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. These results indicate the absence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), and trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) in the tested sample.

LIMITATIONS
This test is limited to the detection of trisomies for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. Other chromosomal abnormalities, including structural rearrangements, mosaicism below 20%, and abnormalities of other chromosomes, would not be detected by this method.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full karyotype analysis from cultured chorionic villi to follow. This will provide comprehensive chromosomal analysis including all chromosomes and structural abnormalities.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Clinical Geneticist
License #: [redacted ID]
